items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: We had a trombone player that played with Lionel Hampton, and he was Japanese, Paul Higaki... it was worse for him.

ctx.x: About what year was this, when you felt things began to get better?

This is coming into like 1948. And see then, every now and then up north you could stay in a white hotel. See but it wasn’t still that much, although I have to put in a little thing here. We had a trombone player that played with Lionel Hampton, and he was Japanese, Paul Higaki, and it was worse for him. So it made us feel that we can go on and make it, see, because like his parents was prisoners down in Denver in the prison camp after the war, and Lionel Hampton took him on and he could play trombone really…
So the music made the difference.
